STA rec_sl,Y
    LDA movers_screen_address_high,X
    STA rec_sh,Y
    PHY                             \ and where that is in the world (BUGS #7): the view in
    LDY movers_screen_address_low,X \ zero page is this screen's now; A = the high byte (rec_sh)
    TAX
    TYA
    JSR world_of_address
    PLY
    LDA wa_x_lo
    STA rec_wxl,Y
    LDA wa_x_hi
    STA rec_wxh,Y
    LDA wa_y
    STA rec_wy,Y
    RTS

\ world_of_address: AX = a screen address; wa_x (16 bits) and wa_y = the world column and the y
\ (movers_y's sense: &C7 at the top row) of that byte, by the view in zero page (its screen
\ start and viewport_left). A character row is &280 bytes: the row is guessed from the offset's
\ high byte (wa_rows_guess, out by at most one) and settled against wa_rows_base.
\ BUGS #10: a mover clipped at the view's left edge (x 1-11 left of viewport_left) has its
\ address left of its row's first column, which is the end of the row above (column 69-79) - or,
\ in the first row, the ring's hidden 48 columns past the last (row 25): placed there it would be
\ 80 columns right and 8 lines up. Column 69-79 is the row above only if the mover is not left of
\ the view (dm_slot = its slot: its x, 80 columns left of that place if it is); row 25 is always
\ the first row's left. Its place is then the address's column in the row below, left of the
\ view (draw_mover clips by x from the address, so it draws in that row). At the right edge
\ nothing wraps: a mover goes on only with x <= viewport_right, so its address is in its row
\ (BUGS #7's explosion, drawn 6 columns right of its x, could land at the start of the row
\ below, and would be placed there: where it is drawn).
.world_of_address
{
    SEC
    SBC screen_start_address_low
    STA wa_off
    TXA
    SBC screen_start_address_high
    AND #&3F                        \ round the 16K screen
    STA wa_off + 1
    TAX
    LDY wa_rows_guess,X
    LDA wa_off                      \ at or past the next row's start: that row
    CMP wa_rows_base_lo + 1,Y
    TXA                             \ wa_off + 1: X still holds it
    SBC wa_rows_base_hi + 1,Y
    BCC row_known
    INY
candidates.new:
STA rec_sl,Y
    SEC                             \ and where that is in the world (BUGS #7): the view in zero page is
    SBC screen_start_address_low    \ this screen's now. world_of_address's first half is done here, from
    STA wa_off                      \ the registers the address is already in, and the call enters
    LDA movers_screen_address_high,X \ past it (wa_hi_done)
    STA rec_sh,Y
    SBC screen_start_address_high
    AND #&3F                        \ round the 16K screen
    JSR world_of_address.wa_hi_done_c2
    LDY dm_index                    \ Y = slot + boff: put_on's two calls have it in dm_index
    LDA wa_x_lo
    STA rec_wxl,Y
    LDA wa_x_hi
    STA rec_wxh,Y
    LDA wa_y
    STA rec_wy,Y
    RTS
.wa_next_row_c2                     \ the guess was a row short (rare, ~1 in 40 calls): the next row
    INY                             \ (BCS here, not BCC over the INY: the common path falls through)
    BRA world_of_address.row_known  \ 65C02 opcode

candidates.summary: ALTERNATIVE (superset of candidate 2; overlaps 2, 3, 4): everything in the next candidate (record_live does world_of_address's SEC/SBC/STA wa_off/SBC/AND itself, JSR to a new entry just past the AND; Y from dm_index instead of PHY/PLY; the dead STA wa_off + 1 dropped) PLUS the row-guess test inverted: BCS to an out-of-line 'INY / BRA row_known' after record_live's RTS, so the common path (the guess right, ~39 calls in 40: INY is 0.2 cycles a pass = 0.1 execution of ~4 calls) falls through at 2 cycles instead of a taken BCC at 3.
candidates.equivalence: record_live: A = the low address byte on entry (the LDA at 2384 is outside the edit and untouched). SEC / SBC screen_start_address_low / STA wa_off / SBC screen_start_address_high / AND #&3F are the instructions world_of_address runs, with LDA high,X in place of TXA, so at the JSR A = (high - start_high - borrow) & &3F and wa_off = low - start_low: exactly the old state at the old 'STA wa_off + 1' (that store is dead: wa_off + 1 is read nowhere in src/ or tools/). The carry from the first SBC reaches the second one because LDA, STA and PHY-free code between them touch no carry. The JSR enters at TAX, the instruction that followed the store. The old Y (the low byte) was dead (LDY wa_rows_guess,X overwrites it) and the old X (the high byte) is replaced by that TAX. After the call Y = dm_index = slot + boff: both 'JMP record_live' sites (render.6502 1328-1332 and 1385-1396) execute LDY dm_index immediately before, put_on stores dm_index once (1321), and nothing in world_of_address or late_column writes it (zero page, renderer-only, decision 34; the interrupt never touches ren_zp). The other caller, list_live, goes through the unchanged first half and the label. Exit state (A, X from world_of_address; Y restored; flags dead because the next instruction is LDA wa_x_lo) is as before. Row test: the INY path was BCC not taken, INY, row_known; now BCS taken, INY, BRA row_known: same Y and same flags-dead state at row_known (LDA wa_off follows). The common path was BCC taken to row_known; now BCS not taken into row_known: same Y.
candidates.relies_on: Cycles: record_live path 17 saved (53 -> 36 from STA rec_sl,Y through the first instruction after the return), list_live path 3 saved (dead store), x2 each = 40 a pass; BCS not taken saves 1 on ~3.9 calls and costs 4 more on ~0.1: about 3.5 net. Bytes +4 over the old (record_live +4, dead store -2, INY moved out of line +2). Page crossings (shipping listing: record_live $A02F, world_of_address $A073, tables from $A0F5): no hot branch crosses a page; the BCS/BRA/BCC offsets are all short and inside one page. The code before the tables grows 4 bytes, so wa_rows_guess ($A0F5, 64 bytes) moves to $A0F9 and LDY wa_rows_guess,X (5 cycles when it crosses) crosses for X >= 7 instead of 11: at most 4 of 64 index values change 4 -> 5 cycles, a few tenths of a cycle a pass; the base tables (27 bytes each) stay inside one page. Everything after the tables slides 4 bytes (not examined). JSR world_of_address.wa_hi_done_c2 / BRA world_of_address.row_known use the scope.label form the source already uses (put_on.going_on). Labels are unique to this candidate (wa_hi_done_c2, wa_next_row_c2); do not apply with candidate 2 (same lines).

candidates.summary: record_live only: no PHY/PLY. Y = slot + boff on entry is dm_index (put_on loads Y from it before both JMP record_live), nothing in world_of_address writes it, so 'LDY dm_index' after the call replaces PHY (3) and PLY (4) at +0 bytes (two 1-byte opcodes become one 2-byte zero-page load). Layout unchanged, so nothing slides. The safe, byte-neutral subset of 1 and 2 (overlaps them; also overlaps 4 only in nothing: independent of 4's lines).
candidates.equivalence: Old: PHY ... JSR ... PLY restores Y to its entry value. New: Y reloaded from dm_index, which equals the entry Y at both call sites (render.6502 1328 then 1332; 1385 then 1396, with no write to dm_index and no change of Y between the LDY and the JMP; put_on's STA dm_index at 1321 is the only store to it). world_of_address and late_column write only wa_off, wa_x, wa_y and the registers. The stack is balanced without both opcodes. Flags at exit: PLY sets N/Z from the value, LDY zp does the same for the same value.
candidates.relies_on: 7 cycles removed (PHY 3 + PLY 4), 3 added (LDY zp): 4 an execution, 2 executions a pass (PHY 6.1 cycles a pass / 3). Bytes unchanged, so no later address moves and no page crossing changes. Relies on dm_index == Y at record_live's entry and on JMP record_live having no other callers (grep: render.6502 1332, 1396 only; sky.6502 and kindcache do not jump there).

candidates.summary: Delete the dead store 'STA wa_off + 1': nothing reads wa_off + 1 (grep over src/, tools/, docs/: only this store); X already holds it for the TXA below. 3 cycles on each of ~4 calls a pass and 2 bytes; the tables behind move 2 bytes down. The minimal alternative to 1 and 2 (overlaps them; independent of 3).
candidates.equivalence: wa_off + 1 (zero page &4A) is written here and read nowhere: the only mentions in src/ are its SKIP 2 declaration and this store, no tool reads it, save_game_zp/restore_game_zp do not handle ren_zp and the interrupt does not touch it (decision 34). STA sets no flags and the TAX after it reads A as before, so no register or flag differs.
candidates.relies_on: 12 cycles a pass (STA zp 3 x ~4.05 calls: the window shows 12.2), 2 bytes smaller. wa_rows_guess etc. move 2 bytes down ($A0F5 -> $A0F3): LDY wa_rows_guess,X (X = the offset's high byte, 0..63) then crosses a page for X >= 13 instead of 11, which can only remove cycles; the base tables stay in one page; everything after the tables slides 2 bytes (not examined). No labels; no entries past a label (grep 'world_of_address *+'). wa_off itself stays (its low byte feeds CMP, LDA and the AND #7).
